Gen.G strengthened its position as the favorite to win the 2026 League of Legends World Championship on prediction market Kalshi after beating Hanwha Life Esports on Saturday, while Dplus KIA beat defending champion T1 in Round 2 of the Swiss Stage. (Riot Games) Gen.G strengthened its position as the favorite to win the 2026 League of Legends World Championship on prediction market Kalshi after beating Hanwha Life Esports on Saturday, while Dplus KIA beat defending champion T1 in Round 2 of the Swiss Stage. As of 9 p.m. ET on Saturday, Oct. 24, Kalshi's Worlds winner market priced Gen.G at 38%, up from 35% that morning. T1 and Hanwha Life Esports were each at 18%, followed by Dplus KIA at 12% and Bilibili Gaming at 11%. On Polymarket, Gen.G was priced at about 36% at the same time, ahead of Hanwha Life at about 20%, T1 at 16%, and Bilibili Gaming and Dplus KIA at about 12% each. Gen.G, DK Reach 2-0 as T1 and HLE Drop Gen.G beat Hanwha Life Esports in a 29-minute best-of-one, and Dplus KIA beat T1 in a game that lasted more than 41 minutes, according to match data on Liquipedia. Both winners moved to 2-0, while T1 and Hanwha Life fell to 1-1. LYON and Movistar KOI also reached 2-0. LYON beat Karmine Corp, and Movistar KOI beat CTBC Flying Oyster. In the 0-1 pool, Top Esports beat Anyone's Legend, G2 Esports beat LØS and Invictus Gaming beat Team Secret Whales. Anyone's Legend, LØS and Team Secret Whales dropped to 0-2. The final Round 2 match, Team Liquid Alienware vs. Bilibili Gaming, was in progress as of 9 p.m. ET, with the result pending. Round 1 Recap The Swiss Stage opened Friday, Oct. 23. Gen.G beat Invictus Gaming, Hanwha Life Esports beat Top Esports, Dplus KIA beat G2 Esports and T1 beat Brazil's LØS, giving the LCK a 4-0 start, Esports.net reported . Movistar KOI beat Bilibili Gaming, Karmine Corp beat Anyone's Legend, CTBC Flying Oyster beat Team Liquid Alienware and LYON beat Team Secret Whales. Sergey Demidov is a veteran sports journalist with over 18 years of experience covering international sports. Since beginning his career in 2007, he has reported on the Olympic Games (Sochi 2014), FIFA World Cup (2014), UEFA Euro (2012), World Cup of Hockey (2016), and Stanley Cup Finals (since 2017).

Before joining RG, Sergey was an independent senior editor at NHL.com/ru (2016–present) and contributed to Gazeta.ru and TASS News Agency. Currently, he leads RG’s global news desk, overseeing correspondents across North America, Europe, Africa, Asia, and South America.

He has conducted one-on-one interviews with elite athletes, including Jaromir Jagr and Alex Ovechkin, former WADA and FIFA presidents Craig Reedie and Sepp Blatter, and soccer coaches like Fabio Capello.

Sergey’s editorial work emphasizes accuracy, sourcing transparency, and a neutral voice, aligned with the Trust Project and Google Publisher Center principles.

He is bilingual in English and Russian, specializing in NHL hockey.
